sources.title: Arundhati & Vasistha
sources.display_note: Linked and paraphrased. Oak’s images remain at the source.

source_transliteration: yā caiṣā viśrutā rājaṁs trailokye sādhusaṁmatā
arundhatī tayāpy eṣa vasiṣṭhaḥ pr̥ṣṭhataḥ kr̥taḥ
passage.working_translation: O king, Arundhatī is renowned in the three worlds and held in esteem by the good. Even she has put Vasiṣṭha behind her.

clue.source_locator: Opening comparison and its two meridian-crossing figures
clue.interpretation: Oak identifies Arundhatī with Alcor and Vasiṣṭha with Mizar. In his reading, the star that crosses the meridian first is ahead.
clue.measure: Compare the order in which Alcor and the chosen Mizar component cross the same meridian.
clue.uncertainty: A historical test needs a specified Mizar component, transit definition, star catalogue, long-term precession model, and search window.

sky.description: Invented positions show what it would mean for one star to cross the meridian first.

historical.reason: Historical dates are unavailable in this demo. Itihāsa has yet to calculate and independently review a historical run.
